feature: Bounded exact Bernoulli differential equations through native and public Python APIs

supported_inputs.q: ascending exact rational coefficients, canonical degree at most 16

implementation.generation: u = y^(1-n); construct polynomial r and C*exp((n-1)*p*x) + r using a backward recurrence or, for p=0, exact integration
implementation.independent_check: Replay every coefficient of r' + (1-n)*p*r = (1-n)*q using the bound original inputs
implementation.public: dsolve with explicit hint='Bernoulli'; default dispatch for supported mixed nonseparable equations
implementation.output: Reciprocal for n=2, both quadratic branches for n=3 or -1, implicit relation otherwise or simplify=False
admission: Original held children are admitted before cancellation
Typed coordinate/native identity agreement and mutable assumptions are checked
Dummy metadata, fresh constant and undefined-function owners remain bound through publication
Borrowed coefficient-list preflight precedes extraction; native failures remain terminal
Previously supported ordinary separable default and initial-condition routes retain their selection
limitations: Nonzero local solution families; no global branch or interval claim
Separate native zero-solution flag only for n>1; ordinary public general solution does not append that exceptional branch
Initial conditions for the new nonseparable Bernoulli lane are unsupported
Rational constant p only; bounded polynomial q and bounded integer nonlinear exponent
Immutable in-process checked results, not portable proof transport or a full ODE compatibility-profile pass

coverage: Degree sixteen boundary and coefficient heights
Typed coordinate/constant identity and alias refusal
Exact and one-short compute, memory and allocation budgets in both phases
